cues.zh: 来回折腾直到多少个The memory model that we've had since the beginning of Java is, well, we have the heap, which is shared.And then we have the stack, which is per-thread.And we have registers which aren't really talked about much in Java because they're not directly observable by the Java program.But with the introduction of closures in Java 8, we now have captured variables.So variables that are captured from an enclosing scope are stored somewhere.And they need to be stored on the heap, because the lifetime of the closure can exceed the lifetime of the method that created it.And this has implications for the memory model.Now, what about garbage collection?Garbage collection has been around for a long time, and it's a way of automatically reclaiming memory that's no longer in use.And the Java runtime does this for us.But it's not free.There's a cost associated with garbage collection.And that cost can be significant, especially in low-latency applications.So, what can we do about this?Well, one thing we can do is to reduce the amount of garbage that we generate.And one way to do that is to use more efficient data structures.For example, instead of using a lot of small objects, we can use arrays or other more compact representations.And we can also use object pooling, where we reuse objects instead of creating new ones.But these techniques have their own trade-offs.And they're not always applicable.So, we need to be aware of the costs and benefits.And we need to measure, not guess.Because performance is a complex topic, and what works in one situation may not work in another.Thank you.
